result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. A supplier registered without terms gets 30, and changing the terms later is saved through `updateSupplier`. All four listings (by name, by country, minimum rating, and single lookup) return the value. The full offline suite passes (176 test classes, no failures or errors), including the new tests.

What changed:

- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier` gets `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30 CHECK (payment_terms_days >= 0)`. Negative values are rejected the same way out-of-range ratings are.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new `paymentTermsDays` component. The existing five-argument constructor still exists and defaults to 30 (`DEFAULT_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS`), so the ~50 existing call sites in tests and `DemoScenario` compile unchanged.
- **`DataStore.java`**:
  - `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the new column.
  - The four listed queries read it.
  - I also added it to the other supplier reads (purchase suggestions, purchased quantity per supplier, supplier performance, spending per supplier, category suppliers). Without that, those records would silently report 30 days. This goes slightly beyond the four listings you named.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: tests for the 30-day default, the 45→14 renegotiation shown in all listings, and rejection of negative terms.

Nothing was committed. The `.claude/` directory was already untracked before I started. One Bash command was blocked by the sandbox, so I made those replacements with the Edit tool instead.
